page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan: left page is a narrow strip of a facing page with marginal text (partly cut, running vertically in small type), right page is the main page with running head, page number, two rules, text, a colophon-like line, and a woodcut ornament. Left page: the facing page's text block is partly visible at the far left edge; the right page: one text column, a running head at top, below it headings and paragraphs, a woodcut ornament below the text.

main_text.head: REGULA II.
main_text.p: Post vocabulum ὀξύτονον & περισπωμένον amittit accentum suum, ut Matth.28. μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰμι, vobiscum sum. Act.16.9. α τις, vir quidam, Johan.21.16. ἀγαπᾷς με; an diligis me?
main_text.head: REGULA III.
main_text.p: Post vocabulum penacutum seu παροξύτονον dictio enclitica monosyllaba amittit accentum, dissyllaba vero suum retinet, ut, Rom.14. v.23. πᾶν ὃ οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως ἁμαρτία ἐστί. Quicquid non est ex fide, peccatum est Rom.1.11. ἵνα τι μεταδῶ ut quid impertiar. Hic τι amittit accentum suum post vocem penacutam.

page.notes: The left-hand strip is a facing page only partly visible and largely illegible; its marginal Greek and Latin text is not transcribed. The woodcut ornament and the manuscript annotations ("Finis" overwritten, the "Hde" scribble, and the signature-like scrawl at the bottom) are handwriting or decoration and are not transcribed. Greek passages are approximate where the print is faint.
